flood.title: Flood
flood.description: Floods occur when water overflows onto normally dry land. They can happen because of heavy rainfall, overflowing rivers, storms, or poor drainage.
before: Keep an emergency kit ready.
Store important documents in waterproof containers.
Keep drinking water and essential medicines available.
Know the safest higher ground or evacuation area near you.
Follow official weather and disaster alerts.
during: Stay calm and move to higher ground if instructed.
Follow evacuation orders from authorities.
Keep your phone charged and stay connected.
Avoid walking or swimming through flood water.
Stay away from electrical equipment and fallen power lines.
after: Wait for the official all-clear before returning home.
Avoid standing water because it may be contaminated or electrically dangerous.
Check your surroundings for damaged structures.
Report emergencies or damaged infrastructure to authorities.

earthquake.title: Earthquake
earthquake.description: An earthquake is the sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement within the Earth's crust.
before: Prepare an emergency kit.
Identify safe places inside your home or building.
Secure heavy furniture and objects.
Keep important documents and emergency contacts accessible.
Practice Drop, Cover, and Hold On.
during: Drop to the ground.
Take cover under a sturdy table or desk.
Hold on until the shaking stops.
Stay away from windows and glass.
Do not use elevators.
after: Check yourself and others for injuries.
Move carefully away from damaged buildings.
Do not enter damaged structures unless authorities say it is safe.

cyclone.title: Cyclone
cyclone.description: A cyclone is a powerful rotating storm that can bring strong winds, heavy rainfall, flooding, and storm surges.
before: Monitor official cyclone warnings.
Prepare an emergency kit and sufficient drinking water.
Secure loose objects around your home.
Keep important documents in waterproof containers.
Know your nearest evacuation shelter.
during: Stay indoors and away from windows.
Keep doors and windows securely closed.
Follow evacuation instructions from authorities.
Avoid travelling unless absolutely necessary.
Stay updated through official alerts.
after: Avoid fallen power lines and damaged buildings.
Do not travel through flooded roads.
Check family members and neighbours if it is safe.

fire.title: Fire
fire.description: Fires can spread quickly and produce dangerous heat and smoke. Early action and safe evacuation are essential.
before: Install and maintain smoke alarms.
Keep fire extinguishers accessible.
Keep electrical wiring and appliances in good condition.
Know the emergency exits in your home or workplace.
Practice a fire evacuation plan.
during: Raise the alarm and call emergency services.
Leave the building using the safest available exit.
Stay low if there is smoke.
Never use an elevator during a fire.
If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop, and roll.
after: Do not return to the building until authorities declare it safe.
Seek medical attention for injuries or smoke exposure.

landslide.title: Landslide
landslide.description: A landslide is the movement of rock, soil, or debris down a slope. Heavy rainfall, earthquakes, and unstable terrain can trigger landslides.
before: Learn whether your area is at risk of landslides.
Monitor heavy rainfall and official warnings.
Know your evacuation route.
Avoid building or staying near unstable slopes.
Keep an emergency kit ready.
during: Move away from the path of the landslide immediately.
Follow evacuation instructions.
Stay alert for additional landslides.
Avoid valleys and low-lying areas during severe conditions.
Do not approach an active landslide.
after: Stay away from the affected area.
Watch for additional landslides or falling debris.

drought.title: Drought
drought.description: Drought is a prolonged period of unusually low rainfall that can lead to water shortages and affect agriculture and communities.
before: Store water safely when advised by authorities.
Use water efficiently.
Repair leaking taps and pipes.
Learn about local water conservation measures.
Keep emergency drinking water available.
during: Follow local water-use restrictions.
Prioritize drinking water and essential needs.
Avoid unnecessary water consumption.
Protect yourself from extreme heat.
Follow official guidance about water safety.
after: Continue conserving water until supplies recover.

thunderstorm.title: Thunderstorm
thunderstorm.description: Thunderstorms can produce lightning, strong winds, heavy rainfall, hail, and sometimes flash flooding.
before: Monitor weather forecasts and warnings.
Secure loose outdoor objects.
Keep windows and doors closed.
Keep an emergency kit ready.
Bring outdoor equipment indoors when possible.
during: Stay indoors during lightning activity.
Stay away from windows.
Avoid using wired electrical equipment.
Do not stand under isolated trees.
Avoid flooded roads and areas.
after: Wait until the storm has completely passed.
Check for property damage from a safe location.

heatwave.title: Heatwave
heatwave.description: A heatwave is a period of unusually high temperatures that can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion, and other heat-related problems.
before: Keep drinking water available.
Prepare lightweight and comfortable clothing.
Check weather forecasts during extreme heat.
Keep your home as cool as possible.
Plan outdoor activities during cooler parts of the day.
during: Drink plenty of water.
Stay in a cool or shaded place.
Avoid strenuous outdoor activities during peak heat.
Wear light-coloured, loose-fitting clothing.
Check on elderly people, children, and vulnerable individuals.
after: Allow your body to cool and recover.
Watch for symptoms of heat-related illness.
